evals.prompt: I have a photo of a Saarinen Tulip Chair I want to use in an AutoCAD floor plan. The chair is 26" wide, 23.5" deep, and 32" tall. It's the white version, model number 150, from Knoll. List price is $2,695. Can you convert it to a DXF block I can insert into my drawings? I'll need the manufacturer and model embedded as attributes. Here's the image: [imagine a front-elevation photo of the iconic Saarinen Tulip arm chair — white fiberglass shell seat on a single tulip pedestal base, no visible back legs, one central column meeting a circular base]
evals.expected_output: A valid .dxf file containing: a block named approximately FURN-1-TULIP-CHAIR or similar, geometry representing the chair in front elevation (seat, back, pedestal column, circular base arc), all 7 FF&E ATTDEF attributes, INSERT with ATTRIB values populated including name=Tulip Arm Chair, manufacturer=Knoll, model=150, dimensions=26x23.5x32, price=$2,695

assertions.name: dxf_file_exists
assertions.description: A .dxf output file was created

assertions.name: dxf_is_valid
assertions.description: ezdxf can open the file without errors

assertions.name: has_block_definition
assertions.description: File contains at least one named block definition (not just model space)
assertions.check: python: len([b for b in doc.blocks if not b.name.startswith('*')]) >= 1

assertions.name: has_all_7_attribs
assertions.description: Block INSERT has all 7 standard FF&E attributes populated
assertions.check: python: all required attribute tags present in INSERT attribs

assertions.name: geometry_has_outline
assertions.description: Block contains at least one entity on the 0-OUTLINE layer
assertions.check: python: any entity on 0-OUTLINE layer in block

assertions.name: units_set_to_inches
assertions.description: DXF header INSUNITS is set to 1 (inches)

assertions.name: dimensions_attribute_nonempty
assertions.description: DIMENSIONS attribute contains a value (not empty string)
assertions.check: python: DIMENSIONS attrib text is not empty

evals.prompt: hey i have this pendant light fixture i want to add to my revit model. its the Solis Pendant from Pablo Designs, 24" diameter, hangs about 18" below ceiling, model SOLI-24. found it for around $1,150. finish is white oak. heres the image: [imagine a photo of the Solis pendant — a round disc-shaped shade made of wood slats, about 24" wide and 8" tall, hung from a fabric-covered cord from a small circular canopy, viewed slightly from below at an angle]
evals.expected_output: A valid .dxf file with a pendant fixture block, geometry showing the circular/disc shade, cord, and ceiling canopy in front elevation (flattened from perspective photo), ATTDEF attributes for all 7 fields, CATEGORY_CODE set to PF, MANUFACTURER as Pablo Designs, price around $1,150, dimensions reflecting 24" width

assertions.name: dxf_file_exists
assertions.description: A .dxf output file was created

assertions.name: dxf_is_valid
assertions.description: ezdxf can open the file without errors

assertions.name: has_block_definition
assertions.description: File contains at least one named block definition

assertions.name: has_all_7_attribs
assertions.description: All 7 FF&E attribute tags are present in the block INSERT

assertions.name: category_is_pf
assertions.description: CATEGORY_CODE attribute is set to PF (pendant fixture)

assertions.name: contains_circular_geometry
assertions.description: Block contains at least one CIRCLE or ARC entity (appropriate for round pendant shade)
assertions.check: python: any CIRCLE or ARC entity in block

assertions.name: perspective_handled
assertions.description: Skill noted the view type (front elevation or similar) since image was angled

evals.prompt: I'm speccing out a bathroom and want CAD blocks for my plumbing fixtures. This is a Brizo Litze pull-down kitchen faucet, model 64025LF, in Luxe Gold finish. It's 8.6" wide at the base and 15" tall. MSRP $1,021. I want it as a DXF with all the product attributes so I can schedule it in AutoCAD. The image shows: [imagine a front-facing product photo of a bridge/pull-down kitchen faucet — tall arching spout, two handles on the sides, escutcheon plate at base, shown on a white background]
evals.expected_output: A valid .dxf file with a faucet block (category FA), geometry in front elevation showing the tall arched spout, two handles, and base escutcheon, ATTDEF attributes for all 7 fields with manufacturer=Brizo, model=64025LF, finish=Luxe Gold, dimensions reflecting 8.6x15 inches, price=$1,021

assertions.name: dxf_file_exists
assertions.description: A .dxf output file was created

assertions.name: dxf_is_valid
assertions.description: ezdxf can open the file without errors

assertions.name: has_block_definition
assertions.description: File contains at least one named block definition

assertions.name: has_all_7_attribs
assertions.description: All 7 FF&E attribute tags are present

assertions.name: category_is_fa
assertions.description: CATEGORY_CODE is set to FA (faucet)

assertions.name: geometry_has_detail_layer
assertions.description: Block has entities on 0-DETAIL layer (handles, hardware details)
assertions.check: python: any entity on 0-DETAIL layer in block

assertions.name: has_arc_for_spout
assertions.description: Block contains at least one ARC entity (appropriate for curved faucet spout)
assertions.check: python: any ARC entity in block
